tier_reason: First-party results (a table image in rust/README.md) from the project's own cross-host benchmark code (rust/benches/ecs/source.rs, sink.rs, Dockerfile). The CPU model is not stated (only the AWS i3en.12xlarge instance type), and the compiler is an unpinned Rust nightly image with --release. It is not peer-reviewed or independent, so it is C, not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Warm-median throughput (median of 5 runs, GiB/s) is 1.06x-1.71x Arrow Flight in all 16 cells (4 schema shapes x 1/4/8/16 streams). For example, numeric with 1 stream: 1.109 vs 0.649 GiB/s (1.71x); numeric with 16 streams: 5.780 vs 5.434 (1.06x); string-heavy with 1 stream: 1.109 vs 0.828 (1.34x). The gap narrows toward the 50 Gbit/s link limit as stream count rises. No numeric latency comparison is given in text, only the claim that p99 is within 1% of p50.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust nightly (rustlang/rust:nightly-bookworm-slim Docker image, version not pinned), cargo build --release, features bench_arrow_flight,protocol,tcp,mmap (rust/benches/ecs/Dockerfile)
corrections.caveats: Baseline is Arrow Flight (the arrow-flight crate over gRPC/HTTP2), not bare gRPC, so this is a proxy comparison. First-party benchmark; the code is in rust/benches/ecs/. The README says 'see benchmarks/', but that root path does not exist. The CPU model is not stated (only the i3en.12xlarge instance type) and the nightly toolchain is not pinned. Gains shrink to 1.06x-1.17x at 16 streams, where both approach the 50 Gbit/s link. Lightstream's timing includes global ordered reconstruction, which Flight does not do. The project is very new and has no independent reproduction.

notes: Numbers come from the full-results-table.png image embedded in rust/README.md; every cell shows a Lightstream lead but the margins are modest (1.06x-1.71x). Metadata was checked via github.com HTML and the commits atom feed because the API was rate-limited: 41 stars, last commit 2026-09-19, not archived, not a fork, LICENSE is MPL-2.0.

tier_reason: First-party in-process microbenchmark table in the README comparing against gRPC. Benchmark code is public (internal/grpccompat/benchmark_test.go), but no hardware, Go version or flags are given, and the README admits the environment was uncontrolled and untuned.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Unitary time/op is 68-72% lower than gRPC (small: 29.7us->8.3us; large: 1.70ms->0.54ms), and unitary speed is +214% to +243% (large: 618MB/s->1939MB/s). Across all call types and sizes, time/op is 46-73% lower and speed is +86% to +263%. Streaming calls with small and medium payloads show smaller gains (about +86% to +176%).
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1.6k stars (1,632); README says it has been used in production for years across tens of thousands of servers

notes: The record's '+214% to +243%' throughput range applies only to unitary calls, so I clarified it with the full range from the table. Metadata was checked via github.com HTML and the atom feed because the API was rate-limited: MIT, last commit 2026-08-18, not archived, not a fork.

tier_reason: First-party docs page with public benchmark code (loopholelabs/frpc-go-benchmarks, now archived) and a stated CPU model (2x AMD EPYC 7643). The Go version and build flags are not stated, so it is not A, and it is not independent.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Per-client throughput is 2-4x gRPC depending on message size, per the page: 32B about 4x (112 vs 29 RPC/s per client at 8192 clients); 512B '2-3x' (98 vs 29); 128KB '3-4x' (192 vs 65 at 100 clients); 1MB is claimed '3-4x', but the page's own totals (about 3.6 vs 1.7 GB/s) are about 2.1x (derived from page data). Server throughput is more than 2,000,000 RPC/s vs just under 500,000 for gRPC at 8192 clients (over 4x). With 50us of blocking work it is about 1,600,000 vs about 400,000 RPC/s.
corrections.hardware: Bare-metal host running Debian 11, 2x AMD EPYC 7643 48-core CPUs, 256GB DDR4, local network
corrections.workload: Echo RPC service (same proto3 file and service implementation for both) at 32B, 512B, 128KB and 1MB message sizes with increasing concurrent clients (up to 8192). Also a server-throughput test with 10 concurrent RPCs per client, and a variant with 50-microsecond time.Sleep blocking server work in goroutine-per-RPC mode.
corrections.caveats: Benchmark is on the project's own docs site (first-party). The hardware is stated, but the Go version and build flags are not. The linked benchmark repo (loopholelabs/frpc-go-benchmarks) was archived on Jul 21, 2026. The 1MB section's '3-4x' contradicts its own totals (about 2.1x). The main results used fRPC's non-default single-goroutine-per-connection mode.

notes: The record's '~3-4x across tested message sizes' slightly overstated the 512B case (the page says 2-3x), so I corrected it. The tier stays C. Metadata was checked via github.com HTML and the atom feed: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE.md), 462 stars, last commit 2025-09-22 (just over 12 months, so stale), frpc-go itself not archived.
